newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS to drop surcharge if fuel price falls.
newsitem.headline: SAS to drop surcharge if fuel price falls.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines said on Friday it will drop the cargo fuel surcharge in April if jet fuel prices keep falling.
"Jet fuel prices are forecast to fall and if they do, we expect to drop surcharges in April," said Jens Justesen, commercial director at SAS Cargo.
"We don't know when we will do it, but when we do, we will do so at short notice."
International airlines Delta and Virgin Atlantic have dropped their surcharge and United Airlines will do so next Monday.
SAS introduced a surcharge of 10 cents a kilo on intercontinental flights and five cents a kilo on European flights in November last year, in response to surging jet fuel prices.

"We have been watching the price closely since introducing the surcharge," Justesen said. "We have been comparing with prices in June/July 1996 and the current price is close, only a couple of percent higher."

Currently, North Western European jet fuel prices are at $185 a tonne CIF, compared to an average for the period March 3 to April 3 of $190.21. Last July's monthly average was 200.93 with the high at $282 on October 4.
